label: STOPP B17
title: Long-term NSAID with vascular disease
statement: Long-term systemic i.e., non-topical NSAIDs with known history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease (increased risk of thrombosis).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: Anti-inflammatory pain medicines taken for a long time can raise the risk of clots in a person who already has heart, brain or leg artery disease.

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.what: Coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease
needs_facts.meets: any of these recorded as a current or past diagnosis

needs_facts.what: Duration of regular systemic NSAID use
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if the supply dates, quantities and directions make regular use beyond three calendar months plausible but uncertain and the vascular history has not ruled out a finding. Confirm how often and for how long the person took the medicine.

options.words: Used regularly for more than three months
Used for three months or less, or only in separate short courses

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown, confirm it before reporting a finding. Use the supply dates, quantities, directions and gaps to decide whether Group A systemic NSAID treatment covers more than three calendar months. Separate completed short courses, a pattern below the duration threshold or an explicitly excluded vascular history gives no finding. When ongoing use and coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease are documented, report a finding and cite both. If regular use for more than three calendar months is plausible but uncertain, including with as-needed directions, ask for "Duration of regular systemic NSAID use". A confirmed longer course still requires vascular disease for a finding. Cite any answer needed to establish duration. Three months or less or separate short courses rule it out. An unknown duration leaves it possible if vascular disease has not been excluded. If vascular history is missing and long-term use is established or plausible, report only a possible finding and name the missing history.
cannot_be_seen: How often the NSAID is really taken, NSAIDs bought without a prescription, and any vascular disease that was never recorded.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm any missing vascular history or duration of systemic NSAID use and review the pain treatment if long-term use and vascular disease are both confirmed?
